name: comp-228

frames.best_why: The full list is open with all three portrait rows and the check on the current choice.

tagline: Pick a person from a list of portrait rows with names and handles.
summary: A dropdown for choosing one person from a short team list. Each choice shows a large round photo, a name and a handle, and the closed trigger mirrors the chosen person.
appearance: A dark form field with a small label above it. The trigger shows a round avatar, a bold name, a grey handle and a chevron at the right. Opened, a rounded dark menu stacks three avatar rows with names and handles.
behaviour: Clicking the trigger drops a list of people below it. Rows highlight under the cursor, the current choice carries a check at its right edge, and picking a row closes the menu and swaps the avatar and name on the trigger.
demo_content: Jenny Hamilton, Paul Smith and Luna Wyen with handles such as @jennycodes.
search_phrases: pick a team member from a list
use_when: A form needs one teammate picked and faces plus handles make recognition faster than a plain text list.
avoid_when: It assumes a short fixed list; for a large directory you want a searchable combobox instead.
customise: The people, photos and handles are written in the file, so swapping them means editing the source; the label and default choice are fixed there too.
weight_why: A select with three short rows and three tiny images; nothing runs in the background.

a11y.note: The label is tied to the trigger and every portrait has alt text; the open animation ignores reduced-motion settings.

issues: Portrait photos are low-quality placeholders and look distorted at this size.
polish_why: Clear hierarchy and an even row rhythm; the rough portrait images drag it down.
